about: FROZEN unseen Deep set (2026-10-26). Written blind to how the system behaves: the pipeline was not run on these items and no model output for them was read. 14 answerable items (each needs two or more separate passages or books) and 6 should-decline lookalikes (not-in-sources or false premise), over the books corpus. Uses Sherlock Holmes stories, Pride and Prejudice scenes, Frankenstein and Alice passages the earlier Deep splits did not ask about. Labels written from my own knowledge of the books, then the corpus was queried only to confirm each fact is present or absent (evals/deep/unseen_audit.json, with the gold chunk ids). Scoring fields as test_items.json: mention_all = strings the answer must all contain. Do not edit after the freeze: the SHA-256 of this file and of unseen_audit.json is pinned by a test.

turns: What is the name of the hydraulic engineer in The Engineer's Thumb, and what name does the man who hires him go by?
items.proof: Label written from my own knowledge of the book BEFORE any model output for it existed; the corpus was only queried afterwards to confirm the facts are present (audit file). Why more than one hop: the engineer's name is on his card in the opening chapter; the employer's name (Colonel Lysander Stark) appears only in the narrated journey to the press, several passages later.
